absent: Concurrency and locking rules for debug, flush, event and paging paths beyond the single control scope shown.
Full byte arrangement and sizing for processor, virtualization and confidential control areas.
Module side handling for pending notification, exit qualification and private paging tracking.
Allocation and lifetime policy for invalidation identities.
Guest hypercall contract beyond patch location and trust call alternative.
Failure behavior of low level synchronization primitives.

findings.text: Host exposes translation invalidation at full, current, single address and guest scope, with distinct confidential and conventional realizations behind a shared selector.

Host exposes requests for nonmaskable, external and exception delivery plus queries for masking and permission, window arming, and cancellation of prepared delivery, including real mode emulation support.

Host exposes installation of paging roots, inspection of processor flags and interrupt block state, hypercall site adaptation, and reporting of entry and exit event details with priority threshold maintenance.

A virtualization operation layer fronts every behavior seen here and steers each virtual processor toward confidential or conventional handling based on its trust character, preserving module ownership where host visibility ends.

For confidential processors many host views report neutral emptiness and many host updates do nothing, covering flags, shadows, masks, windows, fine grained flushes, direct event delivery, hypercall adaptation and threshold and access page maintenance.
Reconciliation of dirty debug state leaves retained breakpoint and status values coherent with hardware while move trapping returns to active and the marker suppressing exits is cleared.
Confidential full and current flushes both use broad extended paging synchronization, relying on module tracking for private state and avoiding narrow queries for simplicity.

Conventional full handling favors broad extended paging synchronization when that mode is active and otherwise uses virtual processor identifier synchronization across primary and nested contexts, while current handling skips invalid roots and otherwise targets the active paging root or identifier context.

Effective invalidation identity follows nested context during nested execution with identifier support and otherwise uses the primary identity with fallback when nested storage is empty, where an empty identity implies hardware transition flushing and needs no explicit action.

Confidential nonmaskable delivery is always reported as permitted since windows and blocking live inside the module, while conventional permission is withheld during pending nested runs or exit destined nested delivery and otherwise reflects absence of move, STI and nonmaskable block indications with software tracking when virtual support is off.
Conventional external delivery is withheld while blocked, while a nested run is pending, or while nested execution expects an exit for that interrupt.
Host exposes interrupt blocking as an abstract mask distinguishing STI style suppression from move segment suppression derived from hardware interruptibility state.

Real mode event arrival is satisfied by emulating the interrupt inside a narrow execution context, where emulation failure escalates to triple fault and success advances execution position and processor flags.

Confidential nonmaskable handoff appears complete to the host as soon as the module is notified, with concurrent host requests merged into the one already held by the module rather than delivered in immediate succession.

Confidential root installation records a shared paging pointer after width validation, while conventional installation establishes either an extended paging pointer with tracking or a combined paging base honoring identity mapping and active dirty and auxiliary state.
Conventional guests accept in place hypercall opcode adaptation while confidential guests remain untouched due to memory protection and their use of a dedicated trust call path.

Entry queries reveal pending event description with error detail only when the description carries it and neutral emptiness for confidential processors, while exit queries reveal reason with qualification and vectoring detail with neutral handling for failed entry and for invalid confidential reasons without error detail on confidential paths.
Priority threshold maintenance is omitted for confidential processors and for nested guests with shadow support, otherwise it derives a threshold from comparison of current and pending priorities.
Threshold maintenance for priority handling holds the primary hardware control context across the update.

Per processor architecture retention keeps breakpoint addresses with debug status and control plus trapping markers, alongside interrupt and exception descriptors, nonmaskable pending markers, and delivery accounting.

Per processor virtualization retention keeps soft block and known unmasked hints, virtual eighty six activity, primary and nested identifier values, exit reason with vectoring data, and for confidential execution pending notification with extended qualification.

Nonmaskable mask knowledge transitions to cached unmasked to avoid repeated hardware inspection when virtual support is active and remains software tracked otherwise, while window requests degrade to interrupt windows under software mode or STI suppression and otherwise arm dedicated nonmaskable exits.

Hardware event preparation establishes a valid pending descriptor whose shape varies with software versus hardware origin and with virtual eighty six versus protected execution while ensuring halted guests become runnable, and cancellation finalizes any prepared state before clearing the descriptor.
Hardware debug status is restored to a reserved pattern after host synchronization so subsequent debug handling never observes leftover guest values.

Software tracking of nonmaskable blocking relies on guests sustaining interrupt suppression across handler lifetime, where misbehavior risks nesting, and confidential merging relies on guests servicing every origin during initial handling.

High order portions of supplied error detail are omitted to preserve entry success, and a pending single step hint is asserted when breakpoint delivery coincides with stepping under interrupt suppression to meet hardware entry expectations.

Interrupt allowance derives from a dedicated enable bit within processor flags, shadow state distinguishes STI suppression from move segment suppression, and hypercall adaptation uses the architected virtual call opcode.
